newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech crown steady after Lombard cut, seen holding.
newsitem.headline: Czech crown steady after Lombard cut, seen holding.

text.p: The Czech crown was almost unchanged after the Czech National Bank (CNB) said it would cut its last resort Lombard rate to 23 percent from 50 percent with effect from June 27.
At 1340 GMT the crown was trading at 18.486 to the mark from 18.489 at the time of the announcement.
Dealers said that despite the cut, Czech interest rates remained high and that there would be little heavy pressure on the currency in the near term.

"After the news I would have expected it (the crown) to have weakened by about 50 basis points...Still the rates are basically high and we don't think it (the crown) can go down much in the near term," said Petr Kukla of Girocredit Bank.

Over the past two weeks, the CNB has been gradually loosening its grip on the money markets in response to an easing of speculative pressure on the crown which on May 27 forced the central bank to float the currency.

It has lifted an informal agreement with banks to limit non-resident access to the local money market and this week lowered its repo rate 18.5 percent after it peaked during the crown crisis at 75 percent.

In the central bank's statement announcing the Lombard cut, no mention was made of the discount rate, which was raised to 13 percent from 10.5 percent when the currency was floated. The Lombard rate before the crisis was 14 percent.
The Czech crown currently stands around 2.27 percent below its rate immediately prior to the floating of the crown.
